question: Two trains, 163 m and 117 m long, are moving in the same direction at speeds of 93 km/hr and 33 km/hr, respectively. How much time will the faster train take to completely cross the slower one?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = 93 − 33 = 60 km/hr = 60 × 5/18 = 16.67 m/s

Total distance = 163 + 117 = 280 m

Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 280 ÷ 16.67

= 16.8 seconds

**∴ Answer = 16.8 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lengths = 163 m and 117 m, Speeds = 93 km/hr and 33 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed (same direction) = 93 − 33 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Convert into m/s: 60 × 5/18 = 16.67 m/s

⇒ Total distance = 163 + 117 = 280 m

⇒ Time = 280 ÷ 16.67

⇒ ≈ 16.8 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 16.8 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Same direction ⇒ Relative speed = Difference of speeds

Train Crossing Concept

Total distance = Sum of lengths of both trains

Unit Conversion

km/hr to m/s = × 5/18

Time Formula

Time = Distance ÷ Speed
